core_requests: A documented ctx-level read-only accessor to the running case graph / provenance of an entity (e.g. ctx.case_graph or ctx.provenance_of(entity, relations=...)): P022 cond 3 currently reads ctx.runtime.policy_context.graph (WP07/WP08 PolicyContext.graph) to prove a registrant value came from a WHOIS/RDAP record of the case.

A CLI/shell path to run a module on an entity already in a case keeping the case id (analyst selection, e.g. `v3lum cases pivot <case> <entity> -M whois_history_keyed`), or scheduling that runs seed reverse lookups after the registration modules of the same case: without it reverse WHOIS by e-mail/person name works only when the domain and the registrant value are seeds of the same scan and the history ran first.

Weighted QuotaBook reservations (units per request) for P334 budgets: a WhoisXML WHOIS-history purchase costs 50 DRS credits, a WhoisFreaks reverse page 5; the module keeps an interim per-adapter monthly credit ledger in ctx.state.

Apply a source's sanitizer keep-schema to cached bodies of non-sensitive providers too (sanitize_body before cache.put), so WHOIS-history answers are minimised in http_cache.db while keeping the 30-day TTL of P022 cond 7 (sensitive providers are capped at 7 days).
Purpose codes in ScanOptions / AR16 (e.g. fraud, actor_infrastructure, defined in docs/LEGAL.md) so P022 cond 3 can check the purpose category, not only that a purpose is recorded.
A case country in ScanOptions / case metadata (P023 cond 1 'BR plus the case country'): interim module setting ooni_case_country.
Report footer rendering of `data_attribution` for sources used (P336, WP20): OONI attribution is emitted as that attribute and in each finding.
notes: P022 whois_history_keyed: one module with three provider adapters (WhoisXML API trusted, Whoxy community, WhoisFreaks community; derived tier community, terms license, default off, run_on seeds, access commercial_only, optional keys whoisxml/whoxy/whoisfreaks with env V3LUM_WHOISXML_KEY/V3LUM_WHOXY_KEY/V3LUM_WHOISFREAKS_KEY). Each adapter has its own provider fragment (key block, monthly request quota scope key, error markers), its own per-source status and a credit-weighted monthly budget (ctx.state). WhoisXML key in the X-Authentication-Token header; Whoxy/WhoisFreaks keys only as ctx.http params (central redactor). History preview->purchase (WhoisXML), stop at the first adapter that answers (setting whois_history_keyed_all_providers to query all). Reverse WHOIS by e-mail/person name requires an analyst-typed confirmed seed, a recorded purpose and the value in a WHOIS/RDAP record of the live case graph (fail closed, SKIPPED privacy); privacy/proxy/placeholder/role values are never selectors (P003 list + additions). Minimisation at ingestion; natural-person values only as registrant_selectors / expand=False e-mail pivots with privacy tags; person names never pivoted. Pre-2018-05-25 records labelled 'historical (pre-GDPR)'; CR32 confidence e-mail 0.7 > org 0.6 > name 0.4 (CR32 rule itself belongs to P258). The Whoxy adapter is OFF by default (setting whois_history_keyed_providers) pending the rule-7 check of whoxy.com's public recent-lookups list. api.whoxy.com got its own provider whoxy_api (whoxy.json of p2-G14-1 covers the www pivot pages only and extensions cannot carry a key/quota block; precedent transparencia_api). FC8 real success fixtures still owed (no team keys): success bodies are documented/synthetic, error bodies real. P023 ooni: terms set to noncommercial (not the header 'open') because FC3 says an NC licence makes the source noncommercial: the OONI data licence is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (evidence in ooni.json and tests/fixtures/ooni/licence_data.md), so the licence gate keeps it off under corporate until licence_allow. Keyless; BR + setting ooni_case_country; aggregation first, measurement pages (<= 2 via next_url, same host/path/domain only) only as evidence for confirmed/possible blocking; www.<host> tried once when the exact host has no measurements; findings info + context_only + censorship (never scored); attribution in data_attribution, findings and notice ooni_data; x-ratelimit-remaining < 50 stops further requests (partial rate_limited). No acceptance golden-path fixtures: neither module runs by default. No LIGHT/ACTIVE variant was required. Registry contract test, P327 lint and ruff are clean for both modules.
